title: Quashing a cheque bounce case - the grounds that actually work
p1:
A cheque bounce case cannot always be stopped just because someone claims they never owed money.

But many people don't know that some cases can actually be quashed when the legal foundation itself is missing.
p2:
A common misconception is that every cheque bounce complaint automatically has to go through a full trial.

The reality is that courts may intervene when the complaint lacks basic legal requirements, such as a missing valid notice, no enforceable debt, misuse of a cheque, or clear evidence that continuing the case would be unfair.
p3:
Quashing is not about proving innocence at an early stage. It is about showing that the case, on the face of the record, cannot legally continue.

One practical insight: simply saying “I did not take money” is usually not enough. The stronger grounds are those supported by documents and facts that challenge the very basis of the complaint.

Knowing the right ground can make a major difference in deciding the next legal step.
